titulo: Perfekt 2: irregular participles: Group 1: the vowel stays the same

aula.objetivo: Form the Partizip II of the most common strong and mixed verbs, in three small groups (same vowel, changing vowel, mixed verbs), and use them in the Perfekt.

sessao.titulo: Group 1: the vowel stays the same

blocos.titulo: Strong participles, group 1, step by step
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: STRONG (irregular) verbs form the Partizip II with «ge-» + stem + «-EN», not «-t». You already know the idea from English: "given", "eaten", "seen", "driven" — German keeps that -en ending on far more verbs. STEP 2: in GROUP 1, the stem vowel stays the SAME as in the infinitive: schlafen → geschlafen; laufen → gelaufen; fahren → gefahren; tragen → getragen; geben → gegeben (given); essen → gegessen (eaten); lesen → gelesen; sehen → gesehen (seen); kommen → gekommen (come). STEP 3: no umlaut in the participle: «du fährst», but «gefahren». STEP 4: careful: «fahren», «laufen» and «kommen» use «sein» in the Perfekt (see lesson 23); for now, just learn the participle. STEP 5: always learn the infinitive together with the participle — «sehen, gesehen» — the way you once learned "see, saw, seen".
blocos.comparacao: English has exactly the same split: regular verbs take -ed ("played"), strong verbs take -en and often change the vowel ("given", "driven", "drunk"). German regular verbs take -t, strong verbs take -en. Many pairs even match: geben/given, essen/eaten, sehen/seen, kommen/come.

tabela.exemplo: Er hat mir ein Buch gegeben.

erros.motivo: Strong verbs end in -en, like "eaten", not -t.
The participle of «essen» is «gegessen» (with an extra g).

blocos.enunciado: Say 6 Perfekt sentences with the group 1 verbs: «Ich habe … geschlafen / gegessen / gelesen / gesehen …»
Write the Partizip II of 8 regular verbs, including those with «ge-» in the middle and those with no «ge-».
